title: UI reactive foundation: replace global renderAll() with targeted component renders and add Preact Signals for AI loop state — no framework rewrite
goal: The current UI calls renderAll() on every state change, which re-renders all 7000+ lines of mission-control.js and wizard.js on each update. For the AI loop (backlog-260+), this means the iteration counter, AI reasoning text, and findings panel would flicker on every tick. The AI loop UI also requires genuinely reactive state (signals) for smooth real-time updates. Fix in two steps: (1) TARGETED RENDERS: Replace renderAll() with renderComponent(componentName) calls. Each component (wizard, mission-control, findings, settings, reports, dashboard) has its own render function. State changes only trigger the relevant component's render. This alone removes the flicker and improves performance significantly. The existing render functions already exist (renderMissionControl, renderWizard, etc.) — the change is in how they're triggered. (2) SIGNALS FOR AI LOOP STATE: Add Preact Signals (~2KB, no bundler needed, works via CDN/import) as a reactive primitive for AI loop-specific state only: currentIteration, aiReasoning, whatWeKnow, currentAction, tierEscalationNeeded. These signals auto-update the relevant DOM nodes without triggering a full component render. Usage: const iteration = signal(0); effect(() => { document.getElementById('iteration-counter').textContent = iteration.value; }). No migration of existing code needed — signals are only used for NEW AI loop UI components. Add as an ES module import. Test: iteration counter should update smoothly every second without any screen flicker or focus loss.
scope: UI architecture review 2026-05-07: renderAll() re-renders everything on each state change — 31K lines of JS. AI loop needs real-time smooth updates (iteration counter, streaming AI text, growing findings list). Preact Signals adds 2KB and gives true reactivity without a full framework rewrite.
generation_reason: renderAll() is incompatible with smooth real-time AI loop UI. Targeted renders + signals solve this without a framework rewrite.
